Which archive a copy came from is kept in memory as copies are made, looked up or pruned at launch (off the main thread); only a copy none of those has seen yet reads its bookkeeping file, once a launch: Strata's own small file in its caches on the startup disk, never on a share.
As a drag of a server's or container's item begins: the content type of Strata's own copy of it, in its caches on the startup disk (never on the server or a share), once per item dragged.
Strata's own store left over from before encryption, in its own storage folder on the startup disk: removed once, when the store opens.
In the `owns` closure handed to FileOps.trashForUndo, which calls it on its worker, item by item as each is about to go: never on the main thread.

In `owns`, the closure made for workers (transfers, Undo's Trash steps), which call it item by item as each is about to change; and in `holdsNow`, for the one item New Folder's or New File's undo trashes inside the UndoManager callback, where its redo must be registered.
`record`, only for New Folder and New File: the one item made, read as it lands (a change asked for on one item), and where the undo of either put it in the Trash.

The one item about to be previewed, checked just before a renderer opens it by path (it can't be handed a descriptor): a pipe swapped in for it would hang the renderer, a link would show what it points to.
Strata's own cache folder for containers' copies, looked at once when a window's services are made: in its caches on the startup disk.
Strata's own cache folder for servers' copies, looked at once when a window's services are made: in its caches on the startup disk.
Only in its `atexit` callback, as the process ends: the test preference domain's own file.
Rename, the one item you renamed: what it is before its confirmation, checked again as the name is committed (a change asked for on one item).

A member copied out of an archive for its preview: Strata's own private copy, just written, in its caches on the startup disk.
Applying the decision you made in the conflict sheet to its one item: whether the item would go inside itself.

Get Info, after a change you made to the one item shown (or one refused): its lock and permissions as they are now.
Space on the one item you chose: what it is, pinned as you choose it, so preview commands act only while it's still that item (an identity read later could be a replacement's).
Space on the one archive you chose: its file opened (pinned) as you choose it, so what's listed is that very file, never one swapped in before the listing starts.
Measuring the one item shown in Space: opened (pinned) as it's chosen and checked against the preview's root, so the size shown is that item's.

A book's thumbnail: its file is pinned the moment the thumbnail is asked for, so a file swapped in before Quick Look answers is never read for its cover. Off the main thread this needs the listing to carry each item's identity to check the pin against (a stat per entry).

`removeEmptyNow`, only as an undo's job across disks ends: the few folders that undo made for its items, removed while still empty and still its own (nonrecursive), before a redo waiting on the job resumes and must find them gone.
Whether the home folder's disk ignores case, read once a launch (the first time a Trash is asked about): one volume flag of the startup disk.
Where git is installed, found once a launch (the first time a git store is made) among the system's own folders on the startup disk.
